'The British East India Company established a pepper-trading center and garrison at Bengkulu (Bencoolen) in 1685'; 'In 1714 the British built Fort Marlborough, which still stands.' The page gives the year but no holding or boundary, so the land is the researcher's reading (the modern province).

ledger.note: 1 March 1825: Britain gives up Bencoolen. The Anglo-Dutch Treaty page: 'The UK ceded its factory of Fort Marlborough in Bencoolen' with 'all the British possessions on the island of Sumatra'; 'The final treaty was signed on 17 March 1824', ratifications were exchanged at London on 8 June 1824 and 'all transfers of property and establishments were to take place on 1 March 1825'. The Bengkulu page puts the cession in 1824 ('ceding Bengkulu to the Dutch as part of the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824 in exchange for Malacca'). The Dutch gave Malacca in exchange.

certainty.note: The company held forts and pepper districts on the coast; no page gives a boundary, and the shape is the modern province.

sources.title: Bengkulu
sources.note: English East India Company settlement of 1685, Fort Marlborough 1714, Raffles 1818-1824, cession in the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824, area of the modern province 20,181.53 km2 and 525 km of coast. The page 'Bencoolen' redirects here.

sources.title: Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824
sources.note: Britain cedes Fort Marlborough at Bencoolen and all its Sumatran possessions; signed 17 March 1824, ratified, transfers on 1 March 1825; the Dutch cede Malacca.

notes: Written 2026-10-24 by the se-03-x additions batch, to give the company's west-Sumatra coast a dossier of its own (the straits-settlements dossier starts in 1826 and names the Anglo-Dutch exchange for Malacca). Two pages opened (English Wikipedia has no article of its own on Bencoolen: the title redirects to the province article Bengkulu). Unsettled: (1) the outline: no boundary or area for the company's holdings on either page (a coast of forts and pepper districts); the dossier draws the modern province as an upper bound; the French occupation of 1760, Fort York and the Resident Parr's murder of 1807 are not on the opened pages, so no event is recorded; (2) the end: the Bengkulu page says the cession was 'in 1824' (the treaty year), the treaty page has the transfers on 1 March 1825; the dossier ends on 1 March 1825; (3) 'In 1785, the area was integrated into British Empire as Bencoolen' (Bengkulu page) is read as no change of state (the settlement existed since 1685) and is not made an event; (4) the Cliopatria Banten row (shown by the sultanate-of-banten dossier to keep Bengkulu in Banten to 1808, and to lose it to the Dutch in 1752 on its reading) conflicts with the company's holding; the orchestrator should cut Bengkulu from the Banten and Dutch shapes for 1685-1825; (5) the Dutch counterpart is dutch-east-indies, whose dossier begins in 1800 and records the gain of 1 March 1825 from british-colonial-empire; that counterpart string should read british-bencoolen (to be changed by the orchestrator); (6) the predecessor is nobody (page silent).
